## Current finding

- No classifier beats the historical loss-rate control on probability scores.
- Portfolio effects depend on the original trading rule.
- Four feature recipes are compared; final choice and evaluation remain pending.

## A controlled comparison

- Same stock-month inputs and validation window.
- Same trading rules and loss-probability weight adjustment.
- Four fixed classifiers; one original per strategy.
- Thirteen originals plus fifty-two adjusted portfolios.

## Does forest selection help? {.smaller}

All 20, ANOVA, pruning and forest recipes use the same months and trading rules.
Compare prediction quality before interpreting portfolio gains.

```{python}
from IPython.display import Markdown
if feature_study is not None:
    display(Markdown(forest_findings(feature_study, brief=True)))
    scores = prediction_summary(feature_study)
    table = scores.loc[scores.recipe.eq("forest_10"), [
        "model_id", "brier_score", "log_loss", "Brier change vs all 20",
    ]].rename(columns={"model_id": "Model", "brier_score": "Brier", "log_loss": "Log loss",
                       "Brier change vs all 20": "Brier change"})
    table["Model"] = table["Model"].map({"logistic": "Logistic", "naive_bayes": "Naive Bayes",
                                      "random_forest": "Forest", "hist_gradient_boosting": "Boosting"})
    display(table.style.hide(axis="index").format({"Brier": "{:.6f}", "Log loss": "{:.6f}",
        "Brier change": "{:+.6f}"}).set_table_styles([
            {"selector": "th, td", "props": [("padding", "0.3em 0.7em"), ("text-align", "right")]},
            {"selector": "th:first-child, td:first-child", "props": [("text-align", "left")]},
        ]))
```
